lines.text: Chapter one. Born in Baghdad.

lines.text: OPEC, the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, was founded on September 14, 1960, in Baghdad.
lines.say: OPEC, the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, was founded on September fourteenth, nineteen sixty, at a conference in Baghdad.

lines.text: It had five founders: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela.
lines.say: It had five founders: Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela.

lines.text: The idea was simple: oil exporters would coordinate their oil policies instead of competing one by one.

lines.say: In nineteen sixty-five, its headquarters moved to Vienna, Austria, which is why so many OPEC meetings have happened there.

lines.text: As of October 2026, OPEC has 11 members. The United Arab Emirates left OPEC and OPEC+ on May 1, 2026.
lines.say: As of October twenty twenty-six, OPEC has eleven members. The United Arab Emirates left OPEC and OPEC plus on May first, twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: That's why the bigger club matters more: OPEC+, which is OPEC plus Russia and other allies.

lines.text: Chapter two. How quotas work.
lines.say: Chapter two. How quotas actually work.

lines.text: OPEC+ doesn't set a price. It sets production targets: how many barrels each country is supposed to pump per day.
lines.say: OPEC plus doesn't set a price. It sets production targets: how many barrels each country is supposed to pump per day.

lines.text: In OPEC+ language, that target is called required production.
lines.say: In OPEC plus language, that target has a dry official name: required production.

lines.text: Ministers meet, often by video call, review the market and agree on each country's target for the following month.
lines.say: The ministers meet, often by video call, review the market, and agree on each country's target for the following month.

lines.text: Afterward, outside sources like energy agencies and price reporters estimate how much each member really pumped.
lines.say: Afterward, outside sources, like energy agencies and price reporters, estimate how much each member really pumped.

lines.say: Chapter three. The nineteen seventy-three oil shock.

lines.text: In October 1973, during a war between Israel and Arab states, Arab oil producers announced an embargo on the United States.

lines.text: Saudi Arabia had been the swing producer, cutting its own output to hold prices up while others overproduced.

post.yt_desc:
In August 2026, Saudi Arabia reported pumping 6.238 million barrels of oil a day against an OPEC+ target of 10.416 million, about 40% under its quota and its lowest output since 1990 by its own count (outside estimates used by OPEC put it at 7.276 million, about 30% short). This video explains what OPEC and OPEC+ really are, from the 1960 founding in Baghdad and the 1973 embargo to the 1986, 2014-16 and 2020 price wars and the UAE's exit in May 2026. You'll see how quotas are set, why spare capacity matters, how US shale changed the game, and why the price itself is set in Brent and WTI futures markets. Every figure is dated, because OPEC+ targets can change from one monthly meeting to the next.
